title: Publication Gap
description: What callers need this node to SERVE but it does not yet serve. The inbound counterpart to morphogenesis.zig's CapabilityGap: it declares both the typed surface required and how to tell whether a candidate port really serves it. A gap never names a handler digest and never names its own capabilities — both are derived from substrate state and from the contract.

id.description: Stable contract identity. Becomes the published interface's id.

need.description: What a caller gets. Becomes the published interface's evidence_claim.

route.description: Literal served path, mounted by the kernel under /agents/<agent>. No placeholders, no query: everything a caller may vary travels in the body under a schema.

reconcile_route.description: Required for a command, forbidden otherwise: the independent read-back that lets a consequence be settled.

receptor_schema.description: The schema a request is admitted as. Must be one of accepts; defaults to accepts[0].

callers.description: Peers admitted to call the port, e.g. "ip4:127.0.0.1". An inbound surface with no listed peer is deny-all.

expect_contains.description: The gap's own acceptance, judged against the body a real HTTP caller receives. A gap without one is unfalsifiable: anything returning bytes would satisfy it.
